rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran through the file's 7 slides (node scripts/expand-md.js output). Every `##` header names the concept or move it covers and asserts only what the body supports: 'Phase 1: Author the skill through conversation', 'Answer from how your codebase really tests', 'Phase 2: Invoke the skill on this codebase', 'Sharpen the skill from what came back', 'Phase 3: Ship the skill personal-first', 'Decide if it graduates to the team', 'What this sets up'. Closest-to-violating candidate: 'What this sets up' is a stock structural bridge heading (chrome, paired with the standard 'What happened:' widget label), not a concept-argument header — it stays inside because it names its own content plainly (the M4 handoff + skills-folder state) rather than teasing an unresolved claim. No empty containers, no orphan mystery, no dropped qualifiers, no unsupported universals.

Rule 16's own Boundary 2 (2026-08-02) permits a body-only ask for light/conversational-fold register PROVIDED the file carries a maintainer accept-note — this file's maintainer block has one: 'Accept-with-mitigation (check_pedagogy.md §56): no dedicated push-back move for a skipped self-critique ask.' Harm check: is this student-facing forcing function actually unreachable by a speed-runner? No — the SAME move (disclose-weakest-part) is re-run as the training's real mandatory forcing function one module beat later, inside a fence: earn-the-trust.md § 'Sharpen the skill from evidence' → {{prompt:ae101-m3-sharpen-skill}}, explicitly marked 'The skill sharpen is mandatory.' A student who skims past this file's optional body ask still hits the fenced, mandatory version at module close.
